scope: Seven starter vegetable types with regional US extension evidence. Local varieties, planting calendars and commercial-scale suitability are not globally validated.

crops.name: Bush snap bean
notes: Cold soil can impair establishment; regional air temperature cannot establish soil warmth.
Nitrogen fixation requires compatible rhizobia; no subsequent nitrogen credit is estimated.

crops.name: Garden pea
notes: Cool-season crop; days above the cited ideal range indicate heat exposure, not a quantified damage prediction.
Drainage, cultivar and rhizobia matter; no nitrogen credit is estimated.

crops.name: Sweet corn
notes: Requires warm soil and can suffer drought stress; neither soil temperature nor irrigation sufficiency is established.
Soil testing and fertility management are needed; no fertilizer rate is calculated.

crops.name: Radish
notes: Cultivar and local conditions affect maturity. No quantitative heat-damage or water-demand rule is available in this catalog.

crops.name: Tomato
notes: Clemson gives 52-90 days to first harvest depending on cultivar, without stating seed or transplant timing; seedling time before transplanting is outside this screening slot.
Warm-season and frost-sensitive (NC State). Clemson describes best growth at 70-80 F days and 60-70 F nights; no daily-mean heat rule is inferred.

crops.name: Cabbage
notes: Clemson gives 60-80 days after planting head-cabbage transplants; seedling time before transplanting is outside this slot. Direct-seeded timing is not stated.

Cool-season and cold-hardy (NC State). Days above the cited 60-65 F best-growth range indicate exposure, not predicted damage. Cold-induced bolting is not modelled. Chinese/Napa cabbage and bok choy are not covered by these rules.

crops.name: Bulb onion
notes: Utah State gives 100-120 days for bulb onions without stating seed, set or transplant timing; local cultivar day-length needs are not modelled.

Cool-season and cold-hardy (NC State). Clemson notes late onion-set plantings are more susceptible to cold/freeze injury; winter survival remains unassessed. Green/bunching onions are not assigned bulb maturity.
